Live: India sends 10 tonnes of humanitarian aid, essential medicines to NepalNepal Flash Flood Live Updates: A massive flash flood in Nepal's Bhote Koshi-Trishuli river basin struck Rasuwa and neighbouring districts on Wednesday after floodwaters surged from the Tibet side. Nepal Police said 157 bodies have been recovered so far, while the latest update said 403 Nepalese and foreign tourists remain missing in Rasuwa, including 203 women and 200 men. Of those missing, 341 are foreign nationals, including 133 Indians, while 62 are Nepalese. Nepal's Foreign Minister said initial reports suggest an earthquake triggered an avalanche that may have caused the devastating flood, though authorities are still investigating the exact sequence of events. The disaster has also triggered alerts in downstream areas, with Bihar reviewing the potential flood threat and Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj and Kushinagar administrations put on high alert amid the possibility of rising Gandak-Narayani river levels. In Nepal, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitawan and Gorkha remain on alert as rescue operations continue, with helicopters and security personnel deployed to evacuate stranded people. Stay tuned to this live blog for all the latest updates.

Video: People run for shelter as floodwaters rips through building at Nepal borderNepal flash floods unleashed a massive wall of water at the Rasuwagadhi border on Wednesday morning, with CCTV footage from a immigration office on the Chinese side capturing the sudden deluge as it violently surged through the border area. The footage shows the sheer force of the floodwaters as they swept into Rasuwa. The customs office at China's Kerung border, connected to Nepal's Rasuwagadhi crossing, is a key route for containers entering Nepal and is also used by pilgrims travelling to Mansarovar. The devastating flash floods in Nepal left at least 384 people, including 291 foreign nationals, missing, according to the tourism board. Among those missing are 105 Indians, while at least nine people have been killed in the flooding.
